summary: Rebuild of M4-S05 for F-37. The operator's dry-run validation (checkOnly, sfskills-dev, API 67.0) compiled CaseMilestoneTrigger and CaseMilestoneService but rejected CaseMilestoneServiceTest five times with 'Variable does not exist: TestDataFactory' — the test referenced templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls by repo-relative path, which templates/README.md defines as a block to be copied into the consuming project rather than a deploy-time reference, and no step shipped it. Exactly two files were added: classes/TestDataFactory.cls, a byte-identical copy of the template (diff is empty, the template itself untouched), and its -meta.xml at apiVersion 67.0 / Active. The trigger, the service, the test and their three meta files are unchanged byte for byte; the factory copy changed no reference, because the class name the test already called is the class name now shipped beside it. No behaviour was added to the factory.
confidence_rationale: GATES.md Gate D row 3 again: 0 unresolved symbols, no target_org_alias, so this agent ran no compile check of its own. The org error that forced the rebuild is now addressed by shipping the missing class, but that remedy is confirmed only by the operator's next dry run (run 3), not by anything this agent can execute.

findings.title: F-37 addressed: TestDataFactory now ships with the step that depends on it
findings.detail: The test's five TestDataFactory references were unresolvable in the org because the class was cited as a repo path rather than shipped. classes/TestDataFactory.cls is now a verbatim copy of templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls and a declared output. The template was not edited, and no method was added to it: the test needed createAccounts(Integer, Map) and createCases(Integer, Id, Map), both of which the template already defines with those exact signatures.
findings.recommendation: Confirm at the operator's next dry run (run 3). Nothing else in the step changed, so a fresh failure would be a different fault.

findings.title: The factory is now a step-local copy of a shared template, which a second Apex step would duplicate
findings.detail: This is the only Apex step in the plan, so nothing duplicates today. A second Apex step declaring classes/TestDataFactory.cls would deploy the same class twice under one package.xml member — a conflict, not a merge. The same applies to TriggerHandler / TriggerControl / ApplicationLogger if the handler shape is ever adopted (AB-M4S05-02).

findings.title: This build's validation rules are satisfied in the test, not in the factory
findings.detail: M3-S01's Origin_Must_Be_Known and Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save reject the factory's Case defaults (Origin = 'Email', no Priority). The overrides are passed from CaseMilestoneServiceTest.caseOverrides(Id) through the factory's own overrides map — Origin = 'Web', Priority = 'Medium' — rather than by changing the factory, whose defaults are shared with every future consumer while this build's validation rules are not.
findings.recommendation: Keep the line where it is. If a later Apex step tests Cases through the same factory it needs the same two overrides — worth one line in the build's test conventions.

findings.title: No local check could have caught F-37, and none can confirm the fix
findings.detail: check_entitlement_apex_hooks.py reads one tree for CaseMilestone mistakes and has no cross-class symbol resolution; check-outputs confirms declared paths, not references; there is no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI. It took a real org to surface the missing class, and it takes the same org to confirm it is gone.
findings.recommendation: Treat run 3 of the operator's dry run as the acceptance evidence for F-37.

process_observations.observation: The rebuild was two added files and zero edits: the trigger, service and test kept their original modification times, so the fix is auditable as an addition rather than a rewrite.
The template already carried both factory methods the test calls with the exact signatures, so the copy needed no adaptation and the shared template stayed untouched.

A skill's reference file listed a template as 'referenced by relative path, not copied into this bundle' while templates/README.md defines templates as blocks copied into the consuming project, and the two readings disagreed in a way only an org surfaced.
Every Apex artefact this build produces now carries its own copy of a shared template class, which is correct for one step and a deploy conflict for two.

The completion-signal question from the first build is untouched by this rebuild and still open: D10 settled the mechanism, Q50's answer named the first outbound EmailMessage, and the emitted service completes when a Case leaves Status New.
The step's four acceptance tests must run again over a tree that now holds a fourth Apex file.
